title: Free AI prototype maker: a clickable mockup from words · {name}
description: Describe an app, a form or a service and get a clickable prototype: real pages you press through, on a phone or a computer, to show an idea. Free.
h1: Describe your app idea, and click through it before anyone builds it.
acts: and click through it before anyone builds it.
lede: Tell {name} who uses it and the path they follow. It writes a page for each step, presses every button itself to check that each one leads somewhere, then lays the pages out on a board: press one, and you are trying your idea.
cta: Try it with a sample idea
try.ask: Make a prototype of a phone app for my hair salon, Salon Rive. A client picks a service (a cut at {cut}, a cut and colour at {colour}, a beard trim at {beard}), picks a time, checks the booking and confirms it. Add a page with their bookings.
pane.ask: A prototype of a phone app for my hair salon: pick a service, pick a time, confirm.
pane.title: A prototype made in {name}, live
pane.try: These pages are the prototype itself. Press one to try it: pick a service, pick a time, confirm. Drag the board to look around; in a page, its name at the top brings you back to all of them.
pane.asked: In {name}, this goes to the AI: point at a part to have it changed, or press {build} for an app that works, with these pages and this look.
made.name: Salon Rive
made.done.note: The real app would send you a reminder the day before.
replay.title: One idea, step by step.
replay.why: The salon’s idea, as {name} turns it into a prototype: what it read, what it worked out, what it pressed, and what you can do with it next.
replay.reads: Your request: a salon, three services, a path of four steps
{name}’s own skill “Make a prototype”, which says how pages lead to one another, and what a prototype never asks for
replay.works: Listed five pages, each with one job, in the order a client meets them
Wrote each page with sample names and prices that agree with each other, and a line saying it is a prototype
Carried each choice from page to page, so the booking shows the service and the time that were picked
Pressed every link and button from the first page, and fixed the ones that led nowhere
replay.got: The prototype, open beside your request: its pages on a board, a column for each step, each one running where it lies. Press a page to try it.
replay.made: An app that works, with the same pages, the same words and the same look: what a client enters is kept, and shows wherever the prototype showed a sample. The prototype stays as it was, beside it.
asks.title: Then ask your own
asks.items: A prototype of a form for our tenants to report a repair: the room, the problem, then what happens next.
A dashboard of our shops’ sales by region, for a computer.
Add a page to cancel a booking.
Show the salon’s side too: the bookings of the day.
io.title: What goes in. What comes out.
io.why: Say who uses it and the path they follow. The rest is decided for you, and yours to change.
io.ins: Who uses it, and the path they follow
A brief, a list of features or the minutes of a meeting
A collection in {name}, shown on a page as it is now
io.outs: Three to eight pages, in the shape of a phone or of a computer
A column for each step, each page under the button that leads to it
{build} asks for the real thing, from the same pages
One web page that plays in any browser, a link to share, or a zip of its files
exact.title: Pressed before you see it.
exact.why: A mockup with a dead button stops a demo. {name} presses every control from the first page and tells the AI which ones lead nowhere, before the prototype is shown.
exact.cards: From the first page on, each link is followed and each button pressed. A page nobody reaches, or a control that does nothing, goes back to be fixed.
The first page says it is a prototype with sample data. No field asks for a password or a card number, and nothing says it was sent, saved or paid as if it were.
Each step shows as it runs, and the pages arrive on the board one by one as they are written.
where.title: Where your idea goes.
where.why: No {name} server keeps your idea in a form it can read. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your prototype is plain files in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and what you attach go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
A prototype keeps nothing, sends nothing and takes no money. What you type into its pages while trying it goes nowhere.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. A prototype needs an AI in the cloud or a plan you pay for: the AI on this computer doesn’t make one reliably yet.
Pictures come from your own files, or from an AI that draws when you ask for one, never from the web.
A prototype shows; it doesn’t work. It keeps nothing between two visits, signs nobody in and takes no payment. {build} asks for an app that does keep what is entered.
Three to eight pages: it shows one path well, not a whole product.
{name} can be wrong. Press through it yourself before you show it.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for.
Is it a picture, or does it really click?
It really clicks. Each step is a page of its own, and every link and button leads somewhere. A choice made on one page shows on the next.
Either. Say which, or let {name} decide: an app in a column is made for a phone, a dashboard or a wide form for a computer. You can look at it at both widths.
Can I show it to someone?
Yes. Share it by a link, or save it as one web page that plays in any browser, its links and forms leading on, without {name}.
Can it become a real app?

Press {build}: {name} asks the AI for an app that works, with the same pages, words and look, where what a person enters is kept. For a product with accounts and payments, hand the prototype to a developer: it shows exactly what to build.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: the pages are written in yours, right to left too, with prices and dates as your language writes them.
end.title: Try it with the salon’s idea.
end.why: The request opens in {name} and is answered as soon as you choose an AI. Then describe your own idea.
